clue.text: Profit from ticket

definitions.meaning: a gain or yield on an investment
a ticket for the journey out and back again

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a yield on money invested, and a there-and-back travel ticket.

clue.text: Back with cord used in alternative plan

parts.note: to back a motion is to second it
string is thin cord

explanation.surface: Someone improvising a fallback scheme that involves a length of cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A second string is a substitute or backup option, from archers carrying a spare bowstring.

clue.text: Lustful Sarah, with Bill, promises to pay

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
AC, short for account, is a bill
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A tale of a woman, a man called Bill and some unpaid debts, with a racy edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacious means having or showing excessive sexual interest, a close synonym of lustful.

clue.text: Actor confused about victor's frolic

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
confused means the letters of actor are jumbled

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victor, as in the NATO alphabet; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: A bewildered actor surrounding a winner's celebratory caper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns ACTOR into CAORT, and 'about' wraps it round V.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap or caper about excitedly, which is what frolicking means.

clue.text: Notts County

parts.note: read as the name of a football club, but taken as 'the county called Notts', whose full name it asks for

explanation.surface: Notts County is an English football club based in Nottingham.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like the club's name; read literally it asks for the full name of the county abbreviated as Notts.
explanation.definitionFit: Notts is the standard short form of this East Midlands county's full name.

clue.text: South African fellow removed hat for a lady

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for African
a fellow is a man

indicators.note: removed in the sense of moved out of place, so the letters of hat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A South African man doffing his hat for a woman's benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as a gentleman doffing his headwear in a lady's honour; here it means moved out of place, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Samantha is a woman's first name, so it can stand for some lady.

clue.text: Overrule Robert hoarding stationery

indicators.note: hoarding means the words hold the required letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone overriding a man named Robert who stockpiles office supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edged measuring stick is a standard item of office and school supplies.

clue.text: Produce egg after fruit for songbird

indicators.note: after means the first piece is placed following the second

parts.note: a nut is a dry fruit
to hatch is to bring young out of an egg

explanation.surface: An instruction about laying an egg once some fruit has been eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small tree-climbing passerine bird, so a type of songbird.

clue.text: Initially, Frenchman eats the artisan cheese

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A Frenchman tucking into a craftsman's handmade cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek curd cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Short-time worker delayed producing pattern

parts.note: a temp works for a short time
delayed means late

explanation.surface: A temporary employee arriving late and producing a design.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a shaped guide used as a model to copy from, a kind of pattern.

clue.text: Hurry around in this vehicle

parts.note: to run is to hurry
about means around

explanation.surface: Dashing here and there in a small car.
explanation.definitionFit: A runabout is a small car or light motor vehicle for short trips.

clue.text: No Republican hit back, as usual

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is written backwards

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: No Republican retaliated, which was standard behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means typical or standard, conforming to what is usual.

clue.text: Natural impulse about Diane isn't clear

definitions.note: a verb phrase, loosely standing for the adjective 'not clear'

indicators.note: about means the impulse word goes around the name

parts.note: an instinct is a natural impulse
Di is a short form of Diane

explanation.surface: Diane's gut feeling is hard to pin down.
explanation.definitionFit: Indistinct means blurred or vague, the opposite of sharp and plain to perceive.

clue.text: Reportedly drunken sailor with takeover bid!

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: high means drunk and a jack is a sailor

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a tipsy seaman tried to seize control.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH JACK, a drunken sailor, when spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijack is an illegal seizure of control of a vehicle, so a forcible takeover attempt.

clue.text: Stuffed conserve in case

parts.note: jam is a fruit conserve
packed means put in a case

explanation.surface: Preserves crammed into a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jam-packed is full to the brim, filled tight.

clue.text: Verse from Iraq aunt translated

indicators.note: translated means the letters are turned into another form

explanation.surface: A poem rendered into another language by an Iraqi relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A quatrain is a stanza of four lines, a unit of poetry.

clue.text: In Colombo, he avoided tea

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man in Sri Lanka's capital who turned down a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Colombo suggests Ceylon tea, but the answer is a Chinese black tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, once the name for the finest sort.

clue.text: Support aircraftsman before he is a pain

indicators.note: before means the piece is placed ahead of the next

parts.note: to back is to support
AC is the abbreviation for aircraftsman in the RAF

explanation.surface: Backing an RAF man before he proves troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Backache is an ache in the back, a specific kind of bodily soreness.

clue.text: Sport is as frenzied in the country

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

indicators.note: frenzied means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Sporting fever gripping a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a large nation spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

clue.text: Comedian unravelled a rope in absurd emotional situation

parts.note: a comic is a comedian

indicators.note: unravelled means the letters are untwisted and rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian caught up in a farcical crisis with a frayed rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic opera, used figuratively, is a ridiculously melodramatic state of affairs.

clue.text: Is unable to put girl into bed

indicators.note: into means the name is placed inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone who can't get a girl to go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannot is the negative of can, meaning lacks the ability to.

clue.text: Clarify, almost cultured

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cultured means refined

explanation.surface: Making a point clearer while nearly being sophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine a liquid is to purify it, which is what clarifying does.

clue.text: Adversely criticise assault

definitions.meaning: to criticise harshly, as a critic might

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a verbal onslaught of criticism and a physical assault.

clue.text: Bring into line, a line, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: the words a and line spoken together

explanation.surface: Straightening something up, as one does a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to place them straight and in proper relative position.

clue.text: Restrain worker on strike

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: Holding back an employee who is taking industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on strike' suggests a walkout, but strike here means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff is to shackle someone's wrists, physically restraining them.

clue.text: Folk music from one American during parade on island

indicators.note: during means these pieces come in the middle of the parade word

parts.note: a march is a parade
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tune played by an American on an island festival procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi is traditional Mexican folk music played by a small band.

clue.text: It flies north-east after little hesitation

indicators.note: after means the compass piece follows the pause

parts.note: er is a brief hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Something taking off to the north-east after a brief pause.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds of prey.

clue.text: Not concerned from tune resident played

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A local playing a melody without much care.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninterested means indifferent, having no interest or care in something.
